elements.content:
Your code has
two paths to run.

narration.script: How does your code become something a computer can run? Meet the compiler and the interpreter.

elements.content:
From human ideas
to machine instructions.

narration.script: We write source code in a language people can read. A computer needs instructions it can actually execute.
narration.generated_script: We write source code in a language people can read. A computer needs instructions it can actually execute.

elements.content: ONE TRANSLATION  →  A PROGRAM YOU CAN RUN

narration.script: A compiler translates the program ahead of time, often into machine code. The resulting program can then run.
narration.generated_script: A compiler translates the program ahead of time, often into machine code. The resulting program can then run.

narration.script: An interpreter processes and executes instructions at runtime, as the program runs, instead of requiring a separate executable first.

narration.script: Think of the difference in timing: compilation happens before execution; interpretation happens while the program is running.

elements.content: A language can have different implementations.

narration.script: C, C plus plus and Rust are commonly compiled. Python and JavaScript are often run by language runtimes. Many modern implementations combine approaches.

elements.content:
Compiled code can
run very efficiently.

Choose for the task
and implementation.

narration.script: Compiled code can offer strong performance. Interpreters and runtimes can make experimentation convenient. The right choice depends on the implementation and your needs.
narration.generated_script: Compiled code can offer strong performance. Interpreters and runtimes can make experimentation convenient. The right choice depends on the implementation and your needs.

narration.script: Compiler: translate before running. Interpreter: execute at runtime. And modern systems can use both.
narration.generated_script: Compiler: translate before running. Interpreter: execute at runtime. And modern systems can use both.

elements.content: THE KEY DIFFERENCE IS WHEN EXECUTION HAPPENS

narration.script: Let us look more closely at the key difference: a compiler translates the program first, while an interpreter executes instructions as the program runs.

elements.content: LIKE TRANSLATING THE WHOLE BOOK FIRST

narration.script: A compiler generally translates the whole source program before it runs, often producing an executable. It is like translating an entire book before someone reads the translation.

elements.content: Interpreter: one instruction at a time.
LIKE TRANSLATING EACH SENTENCE AS IT IS READ

narration.script: An interpreter processes and executes instructions at runtime, often explained as line by line. Think of translating each sentence as someone reads it aloud.

elements.content:
Often creates an executable.
Many errors appear at compile time.

Runs through an interpreter.
Some errors appear when reached.

narration.script: The compiler translates before execution, and often creates a separate executable. The interpreter processes instructions at runtime. Some errors appear only when the affected instruction is reached.

elements.content: A LANGUAGE CAN HAVE DIFFERENT IMPLEMENTATIONS
“Line by line” is a beginner-friendly simplification.

narration.script: C, C plus plus and Rust are commonly compiled. Python and JavaScript are often run by language runtimes. Modern implementations can combine both approaches, and line by line is a simplification.
